title: Compatible lifting of finitely generated abelian group maps
statement:
Let $A,B,E,E_0,J$ be abelian groups, written additively, with $A$ and $B$ finitely generated, meaning finitely generated as $\mathbf Z$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] for their canonical integer scalar action. Let $u:A\to B$ be a homomorphism, put $K=\ker u$ and $C=B/u(A)$, and suppose $K$ and the torsion subgroup $C_{\mathrm{tors}}=\{c\in C:\exists n>0,\ nc=0\}$ are finite. Let
$$0\longrightarrow J\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{\pi}E_0\longrightarrow0$$
be an exact sequence, meaning $i$ is injective, $\pi$ is surjective and $\ker\pi=i(J)$. Suppose multiplication by $|K|$ and by $|C_{\mathrm{tors}}|$ are automorphisms of $J$; the order of the trivial group is $1$. Given homomorphisms $a:A\to E$ and $b_0:B\to E_0$ with $\pi a=b_0u$, there is a homomorphism $b:B\to E$ satisfying $bu=a$ and $\pi b=b_0$.

source.place: Agent-formulated abelian-group obstruction lemma for the chart-lifting argument of Kato (1988), Theorem 3.5, cited by Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, printed p.252. WANTED: Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, section 3. This general group statement is not asserted verbatim by ILO.

proof.text: Put $K=\ker u$ and $k=|K|$. For $x\in K$, compatibility gives $\pi a(x)=0$, so exactness supplies $j\in J$ with $i(j)=a(x)$. The finite-group cardinality lemma gives $kx=0$. Therefore $i(kj)=a(kx)=0$, so injectivity of $i$ and of multiplication by $k$ gives $j=0$. Thus $a|_K=0$. Factor $a$ through the surjection $A\to D=u(A)$ to obtain $\alpha:D\to E$ with $\alpha u=a$. Compatibility gives $\pi\alpha=b_0|_D$.

proof.text: Put $C=B/D$, $T=C_{\rm tors}$, $Q=C/T$, and let $q_2:B\to Q$ be the composite quotient map. It is surjective. Applying the finite-module quotient theorem to $q_2$ proves that $Q$ is finitely generated over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The quotient of an abelian group by its torsion subgroup is torsion-free (Mathlib QuotientAddGroup.instIsAddTorsionFree). Hence [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free], implemented by Module.free_of_finite_type_torsion_free', makes $Q$ a free integer module. Free modules are projective by Module.Projective.of_free.

proof.text: Let $P\subseteq B$ be the inverse image of $T$ and put $N=|T|$. For $p\in P$, its class $q(p)\in T$ is killed by $N$ (card_nsmul_eq_zero'). Therefore $Np\in D$. The rule $n_D:P\to D$, $p\mapsto Np$, is an additive homomorphism. This uses the actual order of the finite torsion group, including $N=1$ when $T=0$; no selection of cyclic factors is needed.

proof.text: For $p\in P$, choose $e\in E$ with $\pi(e)=b_0(p)$. Since $\pi(Ne-\alpha(Np))=Nb_0(p)-b_0(Np)=0$, exactness gives $z\in J$ with $i(z)=Ne-\alpha(Np)$. Choose $t\in J$ with $Nt=z$, using surjectivity of multiplication by $N$. Then $e-i(t)$ maps to $b_0(p)$ and its $N$-multiple is $\alpha(Np)$. Such a lift is unique: the difference of two is $i(j)$ and is killed by $N$, so injectivity of $i$ and of multiplication by $N$ forces $j=0$. All choices here are from these proved existence assertions.

proof.text: Define $\gamma(p)$ to be this unique lift. Zero satisfies the defining conditions at zero. The sum $\gamma(p)+\gamma(p^{\prime})$ satisfies them at $p+p^{\prime}$, because $b_0$, $n_D$ and $\alpha$ are additive; uniqueness proves additivity. Thus $\gamma:P\to E$ is a homomorphism and $\pi\gamma=b_0|_P$. For $d\in D$, the element $\alpha(d)$ satisfies both conditions: $\pi\alpha(d)=b_0(d)$ and $N\alpha(d)=\alpha(Nd)$. Uniqueness gives $\gamma|_D=\alpha$.

proof.text: Projectivity of the free group $Q$ from Step 2 [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] gives an integer-linear section $s:Q\to B$ of $q_2$ and an integer-linear lift $v:Q\to E$ of $b_0s$ across $\pi$, by Module.projective_lifting_property. For $x\in B$, put $r(x)=x-s(q_2x)$. Its class in $Q$ is zero, so $r(x)\in P$; this defines a homomorphism $r:B\to P$. Set $b(x)=\gamma(r(x))+v(q_2x)$. For $y\in A$ and $x=u(y)$, $q_2x=0$ and $r(x)=x\in D$, so $b(u(y))=\alpha(u(y))=a(y)$. Moreover $\pi b(x)=b_0(x-s(q_2x))+b_0(s(q_2x))=b_0(x)$. These are the required two homomorphism equalities.
